behavior_under_test.description: Test that a left join from customers to orders returns customers with no matching orders as rows with order_count = 0.
behavior_under_test.sql_sketch: SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.company_name
behavior_under_test.property: The result contains customers with no orders and order_count = 0.

assertions: The result contains a row for customer 'FISSA' with order_count = 0
The result contains a row for customer 'PARIS' with order_count = 0

evidence.span: "A customer with no matching orders remains in the result with order_count = 0."
"Several matching order rows produce one customer row and count each order exactly once."

llm.feature: SQL: Inner join from orders to customers

behavior_under_test.description: Test that an inner join from orders to customers returns all 830 orders, as no order has a NULL customer_id.
behavior_under_test.sql_sketch: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders INNER JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id;

assertions: The result of the SQL query is 830.

evidence.span: REQ-SQL-06 An inner join from orders to customers shall return all 830 orders, because no order has a NULL customer.
